alignment_unsorted_exception.operation: throw Exception::IllegalArgument, 'Input to SpectrumAlignment is not sorted!'; the only precondition the source checks in this package

alignment_matrix_initialisation.operation: matrix[0][0] = 0 then matrix[i][0] = i * tolerance and matrix[0][j] = j * tolerance; gap cost is the tolerance, and cells the sparse map never stored fall back to (i - 1 + j - 1) * tolerance

alignment_band_tightening.operation: ++left_ptr when pos1 > pos2, diff > tolerance and j > left_ptr + 1; left_ptr is read once when the row's loop is initialised, so the increment takes effect on the next row

alignment_off_band_break.operation: off_band = true when the target peak has run past the reference peak and the next reference peak is still below it; the row ends there

alignment_tie_rules.operation: score_align <= score_up && score_align <= score_left && diff_align <= tolerance; the diagonal wins ties, and the tolerance boundary is inclusive

alignment_traceback_start.operation: Size i = last_i; the traceback starts at the last cell that chose the diagonal, not at the bottom-right corner, so trailing gaps are discarded

alignment_ppm_branch.operation: MatchedIterator<SpectrumType1, PpmTrait> it(s1, s2, tolerance); a float tolerance, a float window from ppmToMass, and a forward cursor that stops at the first equal adjacent distance

alignment_score_precondition.operation: OPENMS_PRECONDITION(!(use_linear_factor && use_gaussian_factor), ...); compiled out of a release build, after which the linear factor silently wins

alignment_score_ppm_window.operation: mz_tolerance = is_relative_tolerance ? tolerance * s1[ap.first].getMZ() * 1e-6 : tolerance; a double window with a different grouping from the float ppmToMass window that selected the pair, so a matched pair can fall outside it and give a negative linear factor

alignment_score_gaussian.operation: epsilon = mz_difference / (3.0 * mz_tolerance * sqrt(2)), then std::erfc(epsilon)

alignment_score_float_product.operation: sum += sqrt(s1[..].getIntensity() * s2[..].getIntensity() * factor); float * float is a single-precision multiply and only the result meets the double factor

alignment_score_denominator.operation: score = sum / (sqrt(sum1 * sum2)); one sqrt of a product, not the product of two sqrts, and unguarded against a zero denominator

zhang_not_implemented.operation: throw Exception::NotImplemented when is_relative_tolerance is set, next to a 'TODO remove parameter' comment; the parameter is still registered

zhang_pair_walk.operation: Size j_left(0) then for (Size j = j_left; ...); j_left is read at loop initialisation and written at line 169, so a write applies from the next reference peak, and a matched pair never advances it

zhang_strict_window.operation: if (fabs(pos1 - pos2) < tolerance); strict, unlike SteinScottImproveScore's inclusive <= 2 * epsilon

zhang_static_gaussian_denominator.operation: static const double denominator = mz_tolerance * 3.0 * sqrt(2.0); a function-local static, so the first call in a process fixes the Gaussian scale for every later call, instance and tolerance. Upstream defect; the port evaluates it per call

zhang_total_intensity_denominator.operation: score = sum / (sqrt(sum1 * sum2)) where sum1 and sum2 are total intensities, not squared ones; unguarded against zero

stein_scott_constant.operation: const double constant = epsilon / 10000, then z = constant * (sum3 * sum4) at line 88; the two totals are multiplied first

stein_scott_inclusive_window.operation: if (std::abs(pos1 - pos2) <= 2 * epsilon); twice the tolerance and inclusive

stein_scott_float_product.operation: sum += s1[i].getIntensity() * s2[j].getIntensity(); a float multiply widened on addition to the double accumulator

stein_scott_threshold_narrowing.operation: if (score < (float)param_.getValue("threshold")); the threshold narrows to float and is widened again for the comparison, so the default 0.2 compares as 0.20000000298023224

functor_naming.operation: setName(<derived>) after the base names the handler PeakSpectrumCompareFunctor, then defaults_.setValue(...) and defaultsToParam_(); identical at ZhangSimilarityScore.cpp:23 and SteinScottImproveScore.cpp:20. SpectrumAlignment.cpp:17 instead names its own handler directly

precursor_window_default.operation: defaults_.setValue("window", 2, ...) registers an INTEGER 2, which param_.getValue then casts to double on every call

precursor_missing_convention.operation: a spectrum with no precursor contributes m/z 0.0, so two spectra without precursors score the whole window

cheap_dp_keeppeaks_shadow.operation: bool keeppeaks_ = (int)param_.getValue("keeppeaks") declares a LOCAL that shadows the member of the same name; the member is never initialised in either constructor and dynprog_ at lines 275 and 286 reads it

cheap_dp_consensus_weight_swap.operation: the one-to-one branch weights x by (1 - factor_) and y by factor_; the dynprog_ traceback at line 256 weights y by (1 - factor_) and x by factor_

cheap_dp_peak_map_else.operation: the else branch compares the two INDICES rather than the stored value, unlike the otherwise identical dynprog_ code at line 265; both branches are unreachable because each key is written at most once per call

cheap_dp_boost_pdf.operation: boost::math::normal_distribution<double> normal(0., variation); a variation of zero is a domain error under Boost's default policy, and pdf's statement order fixes the rounding the score inherits

cheap_dp_int_cnt_minus_one.operation: an int_cnt outside 0..3 returns -1 behind a '// TODO exception', which a caller accumulating scores cannot distinguish from a real contribution

peak_alignment_no_setname.operation: the constructor never calls setName, so getName() reports the base's "PeakSpectrumCompareFunctor"; every sibling renames itself

peak_alignment_normalized_unread.operation: defaults_.setValue("normalized", 1, ...) is registered and never read; line 217 normalises unconditionally

peak_alignment_gap_is_epsilon.operation: const double gap = param_.getValue("epsilon"), under a '//TODO gapcost dependence on distance ?'; the match window and the gap cost are the same number

peak_alignment_sigma_guard.operation: (var == 0) ? numeric_limits<double>::min() : sqrt(var); getAlignmentTraceback at line 283 computes sqrt(var) with no such guard, so the two entry points disagree on degenerate input

peak_alignment_best_score_seed.operation: double best_score(numeric_limits<double>::min()) seeds the border scan with the smallest positive normal, not the most negative double, so an all-negative border reports 2.2e-308

peak_alignment_score_exponent.operation: exp(-(fabs(pos1 - pos2)) / 2 * sigma * sigma) parses as exp(((-|d|)/2) * sigma * sigma): the distance enters linearly and sigma multiplies rather than divides the exponent

peak_alignment_traceback_ties.operation: '// TODO the cases where all or two values are equal'; with no strict winner the cell keeps the zero Matrix<Size> value-initialised it to, which the traceback reads as 'from the left'

spectrast_no_defaults_to_param.operation: setName("SpectraSTSimilarityScore") without the defaultsToParam_() every sibling calls; harmless only because the class registers no defaults

spectrast_binning.operation: BinnedSpectrum(spec, 1, false, 1, DEFAULT_BIN_OFFSET_LOWRES) under a '// TODO: resolution seems rather low'; bin width 1 Th, absolute units, spread 1, offset 0.4

spectrast_intensity_exponent.operation: peak.setIntensity(sqrt(k->getIntensity())) is the whole of SpectraST's scaling: intensity exponent 0.5 computed in float, m/z exponent 0

spectrast_preprocess_prefix.operation: the loop counter s advances on every examined peak after sortByPosition(), so max_peak_number caps an m/z prefix and not the header's 'max_peak_number most intense peaks'

spectrast_preprocess_replaces_spectrum.operation: spec = tmp assigns a default-constructed PeakSpectrum over the argument, discarding precursors, retention time, native id and every data array

spectrast_dot_bias_sentinel.operation: (dot_product > 0) ? dot_product : (*this)(bin1, bin2) treats the documented -1 and the legacy 0 alike as 'recompute'; the following <= 0.0 guard lets a NaN denominator through

spectrast_compute_f_bands.operation: the bias penalty is 0.12 both below 0.1 and on (0.35, 0.4], 0.18 on (0.4, 0.45] and 0.24 above 0.45, leaving [0.1, 0.35] unpenalised

alignment_score_zero_tolerance_factor.operation: factor = (mz_tolerance - mz_difference) / mz_tolerance, and at :91 epsilon = mz_difference / (3.0 * mz_tolerance * sqrt(2)); neither guards mz_tolerance == 0, and SpectrumAlignment.h:157's inclusive diff_align <= tolerance lets a coincident pair reach both. A statement-for-statement C++ transcription of SpectrumAlignment.h's absolute branch and of SpectrumAlignmentScore.cpp:66-101, compiled and run on s1 == s2 == {(100.0, 1.0f)} at tolerance 0, prints one aligned pair (0, 0) and then factor = nan / score = nan for use_linear_factor and for use_gaussian_factor, and factor = 1 / score = 1 for neither

native_boundaries: A zero denominator yields a defined score of 0 in all three scorers, where the source divides by zero and returns NaN; this follows the convention the wave-A binned scorers already set in this module

Both weighting flags at once is Error::InvalidValue in SpectrumAlignmentScore, whose upstream precondition is a release-build no-op, and in ZhangSimilarityScore, which upstream silently prefers the Gaussian
ZhangSimilarityScore's is_relative_tolerance is Error::Unsupported, the mapping of Exception::NotImplemented
A negative radicand under a weighting factor is a checked error instead of a NaN score; it is reachable through the disagreement between the alignment's float ppm window and the score's double one
Unsorted peaks are Error::UnsortedData everywhere, including in Zhang and Stein/Scott where the source does not check although its j_left cursor requires sorted input

Negative and non-finite intensities and non-finite coordinates, tolerances and thresholds are refused; for SteinScottImproveScore the negative-intensity check is stricter than the formula needs and is a deliberate module-wide consistency choice
A negative tolerance is refused by the alignment, where the source silently produces an empty alignment

max_cells bounds the dynamic program and max_pairs the many-to-many walks. The alignment charges |s1| + |s2| + 1 before the matrix exists and each cell as it is filled; the walks allocate nothing at all, so a refusal leaves both inputs untouched. The source has no ceiling in either case
All intensity products are computed in f32 exactly as the source computes them, and every reduction is a sequential f64 accumulation in source order. No reduction is parallel or reassociated

One implementation per header, under the header's own name. The wave-A Copy structs SpectrumAlignmentScore, ZhangSimilarityScore, SteinScottImproveScore and SpectrumPrecursorComparator have been deleted and the faithful functors carry their names. Those structs diverged from the source: sqrt(sum1) * sqrt(sum2) where SpectrumAlignmentScore.cpp:99 and SteinScottImproveScore.cpp:113 write sqrt(sum1 * sum2), an f64 intensity product where the source multiplies two floats, a pair cursor re-derived per reference peak instead of the source's sticky j_left, and z grouped as tolerance / 10000 * total1 * total2 rather than constant * (sum3 * sum4). SpectrumAlignment survives as the alignment implementation that SpectrumAligner and SpectrumAlignmentScore both call, so it is one implementation with two surfaces and not a second port. examples/identify_peptides.rs and tests/comparison.rs were migrated onto the functors; the crate exports no DistanceWeighting enum any more.

A zero tolerance under a weighting flag is Error::InvalidValue in SpectrumAlignmentScore. SpectrumAlignment.h's diff_align <= tolerance is inclusive, so coincident peaks still align, and the source then evaluates (0.0 - 0.0) / 0.0 for the linear factor and erfc(0.0 / (3.0 * 0.0 * sqrt(2))) for the Gaussian one; both are NaN and the whole score is NaN. Returning 1.0 there, as an earlier port did, reports the unweighted score under a weighting configuration.

SpectrumPrecursorComparator was reshaped from the earlier wave's Copy struct with a public `window` field into a DefaultParamHandler-carrying functor implementing PeakSpectrumCompareFunctor; `Default` and the `score` entry point are preserved, the public field is replaced by the read-only `window()` accessor over the registered parameter, and a negative window is now refused instead of producing negative scores

SpectrumCheapDPCorr::operator() writes three mutable members from a const method. `PeakSpectrumCompareFunctor::score` is genuinely read-only here and returns only the number; `compare(&mut self, ..)` returns the same number and records the consensus, the peak map and the factor reset. Neither the consensus nor the factor feeds back into the score, so the two entry points cannot disagree, and a test asserts their equality

SpectrumCheapDPCorr's `keeppeaks_` member is read by dynprog_ and never initialised by either constructor, because operator() declares a local of the same name that shadows it. This port reads the registered parameter in both places, which is the only defined reading

MAX_DP_CORR_CELLS = 1000000 bounds the dynamic-programming cells of one comparison, summed over every pairable run; the source has no ceiling and a variation near its documented maximum of 1 makes one run span both spectra
MAX_ALIGNMENT_MATRIX_CELLS = 4000000 bounds PeakAlignment's score matrix; the source allocates it plus a second direction matrix unchecked
Both scorers refuse unsorted peaks with Error::UnsortedData. The source checks neither and mis-aligns silently

Every division by a value the source does not check is a checked error: a zero Gaussian scale in SpectrumCheapDPCorr, a zero pair count or a zero self-alignment product in PeakAlignment, a zero norm in SpectraSTSimilarityScore::transform and a zero cut_peaks_below in preprocess. Every sqrt goes through checked_sqrt, which refuses a negative radicand instead of yielding NaN

PeakAlignment's zero-variance guard substitutes numeric_limits<double>::min() for sigma, which makes the position term about 1.8e307; the product of the two self-alignment scores then overflows for every nonzero f32 intensity and the source silently returns 0 for a spectrum compared with itself. That overflow is Error::InvalidValue here
PeakAlignment::getAlignmentTraceback has no zero-variance guard at all, so a zero sigma divides by zero upstream; this port refuses it rather than returning infinities

SpectraSTSimilarityScore::preprocess still replaces the whole spectrum, discarding its metadata exactly as `spec = tmp` does. This is the one deliberately preserved lossy behaviour in the package; it is documented at the item because a SpectraST workflow's numbers depend on which peaks survive, and quietly keeping more state would be a different function
SpectraSTSimilarityScore::dot rejects incompatible binning, which the source hands straight to Eigen, and charges the pair against MAX_COMPARED_BINS before traversing anything

The f32 reductions reuse the wave-A helpers: sparse_dot is Eigen's scalar sparse-dot merge and is reproduced exactly; sparse_norm and the dot-bias numerator sum in ascending bin order, which reproduces the f32 precision of Eigen's vectorised dense redux rather than its bit pattern on every build
Boost's normal pdf is transcribed statement by statement, including root_two_pi as Boost's own decimal literal rather than (2 pi).sqrt(), so the Gaussian match term inherits the same rounding
openmp: No #pragma omp in any of the four headers, their implementation files or MatchedIterator.h; no parallelism gap to record and the port is serial. No #pragma omp in any of the four headers or their implementation files, so the port stays serial and there is no parallelism gap to record. Both dynamic programs are inherently sequential in their recurrence; only PeakAlignment's O(n*m) mid/var passes and its matrix diagonals would parallelise, and the source does neither.
module_layout: All four ports live in src/comparison.rs rather than a src/comparison/ directory. tools/check_module_cycles.py derives its module set from the directories under src/, so creating src/comparison/ would make 'comparison' a tracked module and introduce seven edges that do not exist in docs/module-cycles.json (analysis, chemistry, format, identification, kernel and processing all name crate::comparison, and comparison names crate::param). The ratchet forbids widening, so the split is deferred rather than forced.
